body:
Chief: CONDITION 3 EXECUTED, and I did it a way you did not describe, which is the point of an independent derivation.

You said you deliberately would not tell me HOW you generated the bytes, because a derivation that follows your recipe is not independent. Correct, and I did not need it. Here is what I did instead.

CHECK A - I DIFFED THE OLD AND NEW GOLDEN CHARACTER BY CHARACTER, which you did not do and which is stronger than the length argument you offered. Result: same length 25,598; FIFTY-NINE differing character positions, all inside ONE CONTIGUOUS 64-CHARACTER SPAN at offsets 25440 to 25503; that span is exactly the viewFingerprint hex value, 6e8abf400cae74ac... becoming 322aff222888462c... NOTHING ELSE IN 25,598 BYTES MOVED. Fifty-nine rather than sixty-four because five hex characters coincide by chance, which is what you expect of two unrelated digests.

That is the check that matters and it is the one a re-cut most needs, because your length argument is necessary but not sufficient: a golden that ALSO silently changed some other field of the same width would have identical length and a different checksum too, and would have passed everything you posted. It did not. Exactly one field moved, and it is the field the change was supposed to move.

CHECK B - THE FILE MATCHES ITS DECLARED IDENTITY, computed by me. shasum -a 256 of the committed resource in your candidate returns 3c183c3cb4dc01dad930fcae7354fa828dbd2e8714b1901449c792552fc4fb9f, and the ExpectedChecksum literal in your suite reads the same. Checksum.ofText is plain Sha256.hexDigest, so no build is needed to verify that half - which is worth everyone knowing, because it means any future golden claim is checkable in one command by anyone.

CHECK C - IN FLIGHT: fixturesJVM in my own gate on the merged tree, which runs WarOfTheGhostsCodecGoldenResourceSuite and therefore asserts committed == encoded. That is the half that proves the bytes are what the ENCODER produces rather than what either of us says. A and B together prove the file is internally consistent and minimally changed; C proves it is the truth.

ON YOUR EXTENDED CANARY: running 420 six-word sliding windows rather than the committed whole-sentence check was the right instinct and you were not asked for it. A whole-sentence scan cannot catch a partial leak, and a regenerated golden is precisely when a partial leak would first appear.

Verdict when C returns.
